title: Brown hypotheses are invariant under condensed coefficient isomorphisms
statement: Let X be any scheme and let Λ and Λ' be commutative condensed ring objects. If e:Λ≅Λ' is an isomorphism of ring objects, then BrownHypothesesFor Λ X if and only if BrownHypothesesFor Λ' X, with the bundle of [lem-sfb-brown-hypotheses-criterion] and the fixed-universe localizing closures of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. No coefficient admissibility, Noetherian, field, or finite-type condition is assumed. In particular, a Brown bundle for a canonical coefficient can be transferred to any ring-object-isomorphic coefficient without separately proving thickness or size for that coefficient.

source.place: paragraphs 1--2: thickness, essential smallness and compactness; coefficient identifications in sk-lem-brown-hypotheses-generation.proof.md

proof.text: Pull back the coefficient ring isomorphism to q on X. Construct the scalar equivalence H directly, with functor Mod.comap q.inv and inverse Mod.comap q.hom; comapId, comapComp and the two inverse identities of q supply its unit and counit. Its exact derived equivalence d therefore has the restrictions along these two specified inverse maps as its functors. Apply lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible to e for forward preservation of S and to e.symm for preservation by d.inverse. The unit K≅d.inverse(d.functor(K)) and isomorphism closure of bounded constructible finite-Tor objects give reflection. Thus S is exactly the inverse image of S' under d.functor, without choosing an inverse from IsIso or separately proving boundedness or Tor reflection.

Unpack the objectwise Brown criterion at the second coefficient. Pull triangulation and isomorphism closure back along the derived exact functor. Pull a retract back using its image retract. The equivalence congrFullSubcategory identifies the two constructible finite-Tor full subcategories. Compose it with a small equivalent category obtained from exists_equivalence_iff to transport essential smallness in the same fixed universe.

An exact coproduct-preserving functor takes the generating localizing intersection into the localizing intersection of the image generators: pull back each replete localizing test property along the functor and use minimality. Apply this to both directions of the derived scalar equivalence. The unit and repleteness identify the first localizing property as the inverse image of the second. Hence congrFullSubcategory gives an equivalence dL of the localizing full subcategories. Extract compactness at the second coefficient, convert it to the finite-support formulation, and apply the existing compact-object adjunction theorem to dL.symm.toAdjunction. Both equivalence functors preserve coproducts. Transport back by the unit isomorphism and apply the objectwise Brown criterion. Repeat for the inverse coefficient isomorphism.
